name: Leaseweb
tagline: Global dedicated servers, bare metal and cloud infrastructure for businesses
description: Leaseweb is a global infrastructure provider offering dedicated servers, bare metal, public cloud and VPS hosting from data centers worldwide, built for developers and businesses.
about: Leaseweb is not a budget cPanel shared host — it's a global infrastructure provider built for developers, agencies and businesses that need dedicated servers, bare metal, public cloud or VPS capacity with real hardware control. It runs its own data centers across multiple continents and manages everything through a custom Customer Portal and Admin REST API rather than cPanel or Plesk.

VPS plans are the entry point, launched at €3.99–€4.99/month for the smallest tier (around 4 CPU cores, 6GB RAM and 100GB local NVMe storage), billed monthly with no long-term lock-in. Dedicated (bare metal) servers are configured per-spec through an online configurator rather than sold as fixed packages — a comparable Xeon or EPYC box with 32-64GB RAM and a 1-10Gbps port typically runs from roughly $160-180/month up to several hundred euros depending on CPU, RAM, storage and port speed. Public and GPU cloud instances are billed hourly or monthly, with up to 25% off on 3-year committed contracts.

A notable gotcha: Leaseweb raised VPS pricing by as much as 49% on new contracts signed from August 1, 2026 onward, citing memory/storage chip shortages and IP address scarcity — existing contracts were left unaffected, but anyone pricing out a new VPS should expect the current rate to run higher than older published figures. Dedicated server pricing is generally quote/configurator-based rather than listed as flat entry pricing.
policies: Leaseweb contracts auto-renew for the same term as the initial contract period and cannot be cancelled mid-term. Cancellation notice is 1 hour for a 1-month contract, or 2 months for contracts of 3 months or longer; as of a September 2026 terms update, standard notice for new Sales Contracts is 14 days. Cancel from the Customer Portal — the service end date is calculated from your contract term plus the applicable notice period.

Leaseweb does not advertise a blanket money-back guarantee the way budget shared hosts do; refund eligibility depends on the specific service and contract terms, so review the Sales Contract terms for your product before committing, especially for dedicated/bare metal orders with setup fees.
